item.title: 1.1.99-beta.9
item.description:
1.1.99-beta.9: URL Schemes & Boot Stability

New Features:

  • URL Scheme Integration:
    • Registered thaw:// URL events for external tools (like Raycast) and added support to handle Apple Events.
    • Added CFBundleURLTypes to fully implement URL scheme handling for specific actions.

Improvements & Fixes:

  • Startup & Layout Stability:
    • Introduced a startup settling period to suppress restore operations during login. This prevents the "icon parade" consisting of 10–15 seconds of continuous icon shuffling caused by app launch notifications.
    • Prevented a race condition during app restarts that could reverse icon order by stopping concurrent cache calls from saving the incorrect order.
    • Prevented multiple concurrent settling tasks from accumulating on setup re-entry by properly tracking and cancelling in-flight tasks.
    • Ensured user-initiated layout resets immediately end the settling period.
    • Fixed a bug where different apps sharing the same icon were conflated into a single logical item. Thaw now compares the instanceIndex to differentiate them, which resolves issues where clicking triggered the wrong item or caused auto-hide to twitch.
  • Visual & UI Refinements:
    • Aligned the control item hover background.
    • Fixed an issue where isManuallyHidingApplicationMenus could get stuck if a hide action failed.
  • Under-the-Hood:
    • Performance: Optimized menu bar height retrieval with a new caching mechanism to fix cursor sweep IPC floods, and ensured stale caches are cleared on reset.
    • Architecture: Removed redundant Sendable conformance that is already implicitly synthesized by the Swift compiler.
    • Localization: Added a new Japanese translation and updated the Italian translation.

item.title: 1.1.99-beta.8
item.description:
1.1.99-beta.8: Layout Stability & System Integration

New Features:

  • Advanced Reset Options:
    • Added a new "Reset" section in Advanced Settings to restore all settings categories to their default values.
    • Includes a confirmation dialog to prevent accidental resets.
  • Improved System Item Handling:
    • Added support for the Screen Sharing menu extra (SSMenuAgent).
    • Marked SSMenuAgent as an immovable item to prevent layout "timeout" errors and unnecessary restoration retries.

Improvements & Fixes:

  • Restoration Logic:
    • Resolved an issue where apps with multiple icons or changing instance indexes (like Stats) would cause "shuffling" or layout duplicates.
    • Improved restoration reliability by tracking item tags instead of just window IDs, which can be reassigned by the system.
    • Refined anchor directions for hidden and visible sections to ensure correct item ordering.
  • Visual & UI Refinements:
    • The menu bar overlay now defaults to the status bar level for better visibility, only drawing behind icons when "Show menu bar background" is specifically enabled.
    • Fixed a bug where the overlay panel would not redraw correctly after a frame change.
    • Resolved Auto Layout vertical constraint ambiguities within control items.
  • Under-the-Hood:
    • Architecture: Centralized all default values and reset logic into a unified namespace to improve code maintainability.
    • Organization: Decoupled RehideStrategy and SectionDividerStyle enums into standalone files to prevent circular dependencies.
    • Localization: Updated Indonesian and German translations.

item.title: 1.1.99-beta.7
item.description:
1.1.99-beta.7: Restoration & Concurrency Enhancements

New Features:

  • Dynamic Item Restoration:
    • Added support for dynamic item titles during the restoration process to improve layout accuracy.

Improvements & Fixes:

  • Menu Bar Logic:
    • Refined the rehide logic and improved overall panel handling.
    • Migrated the rehide timer to Swift Concurrency Tasks for better performance and modernization.
    • Optimized rehide operations by removing unnecessary asynchronous calls.
    • Addressed potential retain cycles within the menu bar services to ensure long-term stability.
  • Visual Refinements:
    • Fixed an overlay issue to ensure the menu bar tint and shape are drawn beneath system icons, significantly improving readability.
  • Under-the-Hood:
    • Improved the namespace extraction logic within the Menu Bar Item Manager.

1.1.0: Breaking the Ice

⚠️ Important Note: Due to essential internal changes in how Thaw manages menu bar items, your current icon positions will be reset to "Always Visible." I sincerely apologize for the inconvenience, but this manual re-adjustment is unavoidable to ensure future stability.

Localization Support:

Thaw is now available in 12 languages with 100% completion. A huge thank you to our community contributors:

  • Chinese (Simplified): by @PiCpo
  • Chinese (Traditional): by @7a6163
  • Dutch: by @SeBr28
  • French: by @PipaCode
  • German: by @Mutzki13
  • Hungarian: by @johnnybakucz
  • Indonesian: by @volcbs
  • Italian: by @zichichi
  • Korean: by @YuriHan
  • Spanish: by @diazdesandi
  • Thai: by @priesdelly

Changes and Fixes:

  • Multi-Monitor Support: Improved app menu hiding logic to correctly account for screen edges and active menu bars across multiple monitors.
  • Ultra-wide Monitor Fix: Resolved an issue where menu bar items were incorrectly included in calculations, which previously caused "Hidden" and Always Hidden" items to appear incorrectly on the left side of ultra-wide screens.
  • Refined Notch Detection: Implemented auxiliaryTopLeftArea for more accurate notch detection and added an option to enable the IceBar only on displays with a notch.
  • Immediate UI Updates: Menubar shapes (split/full) now update instantly when settings are changed, eliminating the previous 30-second delay.
  • Display-Specific Layouts: Fixed an issue where menu bar items from primary displays were incorrectly included in trailing path calculations for external monitors.
  • Performance Optimizations: Reduced CPU usage by debouncing image cache updates, adding polling delays, and skipping background timer tasks when panels are hidden.
  • Simplified Settings: Removed the redundant "temporary item delay" setting as the smart rehide logic now handles these cases automatically.
  • Thaw Bar Scaling Fix: Resolved a scaling issue in the Thaw Bar by clamping the menu bar content height and capping item height to ensure consistent rendering.
  • New Interaction: Added the ability to double-click directly on the menu bar to reveal the "Always Hidden" section.

1.0.0: The Official Release

Thaw has reached its first stable milestone! This release consolidates all the progress from the beta period into a polished, reliable menu bar manager.

Latest Improvements (since beta 4):

  • Enhanced Reliability: Stabilized HIDEventManager logic to prevent "show on hover" and "show on click" from stopping after repeated use and prevent saving chevron divider position which could leave Thaw in an unusable state.
  • UI Polish: Condensed the menu bar tooltip for a cleaner look and added explicit double-click instructions.
  • System Safety: Improved thread safety by synchronizing access to the cursor hide count.
  • Apple Menu Fix: Refined synthetic press offsets to ensure Thaw never accidentally triggers the Apple menu.

Highlights from the Journey to 1.0:

  • The Big Thaw: Successfully forked and rebranded with a new identity, app icon, and independent bundle ID (com.stonerl.Thaw).
  • Ice Migration: Built-in support to import your old settings and control item positions from Ice.
  • Advanced Control: Introduced "Double-Click to Reveal" for always-hidden items and "Smart Rehide" strategies.
  • Modern macOS Support: Optimized for stability on macOS 26.
  • Performance: Faster icon caching, display-aware state refreshing, and thread-safe operations.

Known Issues:

If you are currently on macOS 14 or 15, please be aware that Thaw currently has some known bugs regarding temporary icons in the floating Thaw bar.

I am actively investigating these issues and will release a fix as soon as possible. You can track the progress of this issue here: GitHub Issue #1.

Thank you for all the feedback during the beta period that made this release possible!
